document.abstract: Innovations in raster graphics technology have led to the development of tunrkey computer graphics systems that combine interactive graphics and digital image processing. These interactive picture processing systems provide hardware and software necessary for input, creation, manipulation, storage and output of visual images. Interactive picture processing systems have evolved from traditional visual communications media, such as painting, paper, pencils, printing, photography, mechanical typesetting, film, and video. This revolution has changed the emphasis of computer graphics from numbers-intensive to art-intensive devices.

authors.bio: Alan L. Bridges graduated from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1972 with a Bachelor's Degree in Physics and earned his Master's Degree in Physics from that institution in 1974. Honors received: Sigma Pi Sigma, National Physics Honorary, 1974: Who's Who in the South/Southwest, 1982–83; and Who's Who in Frontier Science and Technology, 1982–83. He is affiliated with Via Video, Inc., Cupertino, California. Current research areas include computer graphics, artificial intelligence for tutoring or training systems, and speech recognition. Working in various microcomputer technology areas, including technology forecasting for last four years. Working actively with Via Video since 1982 (working in graphics area actively for two years before).
